question: Q-F1
claim: Rule: the n-th partial of the open B-flat trumpet sounds (and is written) 12*log2(n) semitones above C3 (p1=C3/MIDI48, p2=C4/60, p3=G4/67, p4=C5/72, p5=E5/76, p6=G5/79, p7=Bb5(flat)/82, p8=C6/84, p9=D6/86, p10=E6/88, p12=G6/91); a valve fingering lowering L semitones (1=2, 2=1, 3=3, additive) plays written pitch = partial pitch - L, so partial = round(2^((MIDI-48+L)/12)).

question: Q-F3
claim: Intonation reason: valve tubes are cut for the open horn, so a combination adds tubing computed on the unlengthened tube; the real second valve adds length to an already lengthened tube, so combinations come out short = sharp; the third slide cannot be tuned for everything, so design is a compromise (1 and 2 slightly flat, 3 alone very flat, to make combinations less sharp).
